Summarize1: In Psalm 138, David praises the Lord with all his heart and declares his faithfulness. He acknowledges that God has answered his prayers and given him strength. David wants all the kings of the earth to praise the Lord and sing of His ways. Despite his troubles, David trusts that God will protect him and ultimately vindicate him. He asks God to continue His love and not abandon His works.
Summarize2: In this passage, the Sovereign Lord mourns the fall of Egypt and its ruler, Pharaoh. The Lord compares Egypt to a great cedar tree that was brought down to the realm of the dead, along with other trees from Eden. Despite its splendor and majesty, Egypt will also be brought down to lie among those killed by the sword. The Lord identifies Pharaoh and his hordes as the subject of this prophecy.
Summarize3: In 2 Corinthians 10:12-18, Paul advises against comparing ourselves to others, boasting beyond what is appropriate, or taking credit for someone else's work. Instead, he encourages boasting in the Lord, recognizing that it is God's approval that truly matters.
